name: Snap-on Inc
moat_justification: Strong moat: dominant (~60%) share of US mobile tool distribution through a franchise van network whose weekly in-person, consultative sales are notoriously sticky; a century-old premium brand with proven pricing power (gross margin above 50%); and a captive Financial Services arm that finances both franchisees and technicians and locks the channel together. Diagnostics/repair-information adds software and data exposure. Erosion forces are real but slow: franchisee dependence, discretionary big-ticket demand tied to technician confidence, lower-cost premium-price competition, the EV/ADAS product shift, finance-receivable credit cycles, and mature end markets growing under 2% on a 3-yr view.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.2%) vs bull-case tier C (10.5%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality premium tool franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $367.25 the weighted IRR is only 8.68% (Tier D; bear-to-bull band D to C, sized to the bear end; IV@15% $178.29); it clears the 15% hurdle only at or below $178.29, under half the current price.
moat_for: ~60% share of US mobile tool distribution; franchise van network with sticky weekly in-person sales
Premium brand with proven pricing power — gross margin above 50%
Captive Financial Services flywheel financing franchisees and technicians, locking in the channel
Diagnostics and repair-information systems (software, data, OEM dealership tools) diversify beyond hand tools
Net cash balance sheet; owner's earnings positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years
moat_against: Franchisee dependence — franchisee failure hits sales, collections and finance receivables
Big-ticket tool demand is discretionary and moves with technician confidence and hours
Premium pricing faces lower-cost rivals (Harbor Freight, Milwaukee, Matco/Cornwell)
EV/ADAS shift needs constant diagnostics reinvestment; fewer mechanical repairs per vehicle over time
Captive finance carries credit-cycle risk — loan-loss provisions rise in downturns
Mature end markets — 3-yr revenue CAGR under 2%
